considered: The heavy queue's Entry, its start rule (neutral/queue.rs, reused unchanged per resource), its place-keeping and its waiter loop are reused; resources are fields on the entry and filters over the one queue, not a second queue or a second path; a factorium.toml [resources] table and a --for on exclusive were written first and deleted when the issue moved resources into host settings and holds into worker hold
author: claude-code:0327310b-759b-5013-83c5-29c6192ac764:opus
cut: In crates/domain/src/heavy.rs and crates/factorium/src/heavy.rs, use hold_for.is_some() as the hold marker throughout Job, Enqueue, HeavyQueued and Entry, deriving the existing hold flag in the JSON views, and drop the self-ID check in Queue::covered because the command and hold predicates already distinguish them. In crates/factorium/src/heavy.rs and crates/factorium/src/doctor.rs, share the scan that finds running named-resource entries with a gone holder. In crates/factorium/src/owner.rs, build holds and waits_for directly from borrowed, worker-filtered holdings, deleting the intermediate cloned vectors and tuple passes.
answer: Made all three: Entry::is_hold() derives from hold_for (the hold field is gone from Job, Enqueue, HeavyQueued and Entry; Holding.hold is derived), covered drops the self-id check; App::gone_holders is the one scan doctor and the tick's give_back share; workers lists the resources whose holders or waiting include the worker, no cloned vectors
